A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same study. Their main text, figures, tables, and complete appendices are readable and support comparison, including matching material moved or renumbered in v2.

before.justification: V1 reports original model-to-brain alignment analyses, linguistic benchmark evaluations, and architectural and initialization experiments using previously published datasets.

after.justification: V2 retains those original analyses and adds SmolLM2-360M evaluations and a comparison of alignment with the language network and early visual cortex.

M1.justification: The functional-localization procedure, default selection of 128 units, ridge-regression encoding, and brain-alignment scoring remain unchanged. SmolLM2 is evaluated using the existing framework. The expanded behavioral-scoring description documents an existing analysis.

E1.justification: Appendix J extends the evaluated neural targets to early visual cortex V1 using PEREIRA2018. The existing neural datasets, behavioral dataset, language-modeling data, and linguistic competence tasks are retained; the SmolLM2 replication reuses these benchmarks.

E2.justification: The architecture comparison retains the linear/MLP, recurrent, pooling, and Transformer alternatives. The trained, untrained, and random-token controls and scoring-metric comparisons are also retained. SmolLM2 is evaluated as a separate replication of the analysis.

E3.justification: V2 adds evaluation of SmolLM2-360M at 16 checkpoints from 250B to 4T tokens, spaced every 250B tokens, and a regional control using 14M, 70M, and 160M Pythia models. The existing Pythia checkpoint schedule, localization settings, metrics, and contextualization tests remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendix F adds a replication testing generality beyond the Pythia family. Appendix J and Figure 11 add a regional-specificity control comparing language-network and visual-cortex alignment during training. These introduce substantial robustness questions beyond the retained architecture, initialization, contextualization, and unit-count analyses.

E5.justification: V2 Figure 2 explicitly states that error bars across its subplots report five random initializations; v1 Figure 3 specified five initializations for the architecture comparison. This expands the reported run information without establishing additional runs. The existing cross-validation, noise-ceiling estimation, and Wilcoxon test are retained.

E6.justification: Tables 2–3 add SmolLM2 results across 250B–4T tokens, and Figure 11 adds language-network versus V1 trajectories. For example, the reported SmolLM2 average brain alignment is 0.50 at 250B and 0.54 at 4T. Existing Pythia results and consistency scores are retained. New Table 3 has unexplained average/component discrepancies: at 3T, its six functional scores average 0.40, while Avg Functional is 0.50.

T1.justification: The mathematical descriptions of normalization, regression-based alignment, CKA, and RSA are retained. No substantive mathematical definitions, derivations, theorems, or proofs are added or removed.

C1.justification: The principal claims remain: context integration supports untrained alignment, formal competence tracks alignment more closely, alignment plateaus early, behavioral relationships weaken later, model size is unreliable after controlling feature count, and neural benchmarks remain unsaturated. V2 changes emphasis and adds supporting evidence without redefining these contributions.

C2.justification: Beyond retaining the earlier future-work discussion, v2 adds an English-only applicability limitation and explains why available recordings cannot adequately test higher cognitive networks. It interprets the new V1 control as evidence of linguistic specificity and acknowledges that SmolLM2's coarse checkpoints cannot test early alignment emergence. These substantially expand the interpretation and boundaries of the findings.

D1.justification: Section 5.3 newly explains behavioral alignment as correlation between word surprisal and average reading time, including summing losses across tokens within a word. Appendix A.2 documents 180 participants and 10 stories for the retained FUTRELL2018 analysis. V2 also adds a project-page address.

R1.justification: The conclusion adds explicit positioning against Oota et al. and the already-cited Hosseini et al. V2 adds references supporting SmolLM2, reading-time analysis, and cross-language discussion, while removing several vision and specialization references. The AlKhamissi 2024-to-2025 citation is a publication update to the same work.

P1.justification: V2 reorganizes the manuscript into numbered sections and lettered appendices, moves functional localization into Methods, groups the principal findings under Results, and moves initialization and model-size discussions into appendices. It also expands introductory, behavioral, and concluding explanations and adds dedicated limitations and ethics sections.

P2.justification: V2 changes typesetting and substantially redistributes displays: Table 1 and v1 Figure 2 move to the appendix, v1 Figure 4 is split between v2 Figures 3 and 7, and the model-size plot becomes Figure 12. It adds Tables 2–3 and Figure 11 and removes Table 1's Context column. The other existing plot graphics are retained.

improvement.justification: The visual-cortex control, explicit behavioral-scoring details, and fuller limitations make the retained findings easier to assess and provide a modest overall improvement. The SmolLM2 replication offers only partial corroboration because its checkpoints miss early training, and unexplained discrepancies between component scores and averages in Table 3 weaken that addition. These limitations constrain the strength of the overall gain.
